correctness.rationale: The posterior information matrix is exactly \(S_h=P^{-1}+r^{-1}hh^{\mathsf T}\). Its trace is direction-independent. In two dimensions, at fixed positive trace, spectral condition number is strictly decreasing in determinant. The determinant lemma reduces direction optimization to maximizing \(h^{\mathsf T}Ph\), whose unique maximizers are the two signs of the largest-eigenvalue eigenvector because \(L>\mu\). The resulting posterior eigenvalues are \(Lr/(L+r)\) and \(\mu\), yielding the stated closed form, unique isotropy noise, and exact prior-worsening threshold. The packaged rational checker verifies a nontrivial equality and reversal example.

originality.rationale: The largest-error-direction sensor heuristic is explicitly treated as prior work, as are trace/MMSE and log-determinant Kalman sensor design and generic condition-number-aware symmetric rank-one updates. The final claim is narrower and different: a complete fixed-noise two-dimensional posterior condition-number law, its unique exact isotropy noise, and the sharp overmeasurement regime where the condition-optimal posterior becomes more ill-conditioned than the prior. Targeted semantic, alias, and exact-form searches did not locate this complete statement. Plausible older measurement-design and rank-one-update sources are retained as residual risks rather than declared noncovering without evidence.
residual_risks: Herring and Melsa's 1974 “Optimum measurements for estimation” is a plausible older source for an equivalent two-state measurement-direction calculation, but its full body was not available through the inspected route.

Wolkowicz's generic rank-one conditioning theory may contain an algebraically equivalent fixed-size extremum under quasi-Newton terminology; the inspected material establishes nearby theory but did not resolve the full implication comparison.

The condition-number objective is less standard in Kalman sensor design than trace, determinant, or maximal-eigenvalue criteria, so equivalent older work may be indexed under ellipsoid eccentricity or information-matrix terminology.

value.rationale: Posterior covariance condition number is a natural scale-free measure of confidence-ellipsoid anisotropy. The theorem gives a complete classification of the smallest nontrivial scalar-measurement design problem and separates anisotropy from total uncertainty: there is a unique noise level giving exact isotropy, and measurements made even more accurate beyond that point eventually make the posterior more ill-conditioned than the prior while continuing to reduce covariance. The exact reversal threshold is a motivated sensor-design boundary rather than an arbitrary two-by-two identity.
